deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page: no derivations, formulas or computations. Folio 20 is part of Gauss's running list of new books, almost certainly acquisitions or new arrivals relevant to him and the Göttingen library or reading circle. It continues the 'Neue Bücher von 1823 / 1824' lists on the previous page. The page number '20' is pencilled at top left.

The upper block appears to belong to c. 1824–1825:
- Journal de l'École polytechnique, Cahier 19.
- J.-B. Biot, Recherches sur plusieurs points de l'astronomie égyptienne (1823).
- N. Halma, Examen et explication du zodiaque de Denderah, parts 1–3 and supplement (1822).
- Fanny Tarnow, Lebensbilder.
- Friedrich Jacobs, Erzählungen, vol. 2.
- F. H. Jacobi, Auserlesener Briefwechsel (1825–27).
- Wilh. Meinecke, Allgemeines Lehrbuch der Geographie von Europa, 730 pp., Erfurt, Keyser, with a price.
- Tomás de Morla, Lehrbuch der Artilleriewissenschaft, translated from the Spanish by J. G. von Hoyer, part 2, 758 pp., Leipzig, Barth, with a price; 2nd revised and enlarged edition.
- Gustav Schilling, Gefährten, parts 1–2.

Then comes a ruled heading '1840' and a second block:
- Hülsse, Die Sterblichkeitsverhältnisse in Leipzig (1839).
- Souvenirs of a Summer in Germany, 2 vols. (1837).
- Cauchy, Exercices d'analyse et de physique mathématique, livraisons 1–9 (Paris 1839–40).
- Mémoires de l'Académie Royale des Sciences de l'Institut de France, T. XI (for 1832).
- Cauchy, Nouveaux exercices de mathématiques, livraisons 1–8 (Prague 1835–36).
- de Pambour, Theory of the Steam Engine (London 1839).
- N. Wood, Practical Treatise on Rail-roads (London 1838).
- Fr. v. Raumer, Italien; Beiträge zur Kenntniss dieses Landes (Leipzig 1840, 2 vols., octavo).

The only numerical content is page counts, years, volume numbers and prices (Thaler/Groschen-type amounts). Nothing is computed from them.

Historically, the list documents Gauss's interests: mathematics (Cauchy), astronomy and history (Biot, Halma on the Dendera zodiac), mortality statistics (relevant to his widows' fund work of the 1840s), railways and steam engines, geography, and literature. The next page is a separate set of accounts (names with sums).

results.what: Bibliographic list of newly acquired/noted books (c. 1824–25 and 1840), including Cauchy's Exercices, Biot on Egyptian astronomy, Hülsse on Leipzig mortality, Pambour and Wood on engineering

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely bibliographic, with no mathematics. Gauss's interest in Cauchy, Biot and mortality statistics (in connection with the Göttingen widows' fund) is already well documented.
transcription_corrections: The pencilled page number '20' at top left is omitted in the transcription.
The Meineke price is written roughly '1 R 12 m' (or 'gr'). The currency abbreviations are uncertain; best read as a Thaler-and-Groschen-type price.
The Morla entry price is perhaps '4 R 12 m' (or '4°'), not '4r 12 m'. The sense is a price, not 'Theil 4'.

'Memoires de l'Acad. Roy. de France T. 1832 T. XI': the first 'T.' looks more like a superscript abbreviation (perhaps 'P.' or 'T.'). The intended work is the Mémoires de l'Académie Royale des Sciences de l'Institut de France, tome XI (année 1832).
The marginal mark before the Raumer entry looks like '2.' or '1/2' set off by vertical strokes.
'Hülsse' is correctly read: Julius Ambrosius Hülße, Die Sterblichkeitsverhältnisse in Leipzig, 1839.
'Meineke' is probably 'Meinecke' (Wilhelm Meinecke); the hand is ambiguous.
